This review uses only SPEC.md, the authored snapback/schema.q, the installed snapback4 README, and installed CLI guides and generated results. The guide start and guide security --full were read first. The security loop was initial check → answer its questionnaire from the spec → author independent invariants → check → test --fixture-only → audit. No rules, operations, comments, imports, or other existing non-invariant source lines were changed. No application server was started manually.

## Interpretation of the specification

The explicit privacy boundaries are ownership for exhibitors and club membership for leaders. An exhibitor role does not grant access to another exhibitor's animal, even in the same club. A leader's role does not grant access to other clubs, even when another leader can read those entries. Both leaders of a club may read its entries. The barn office has a fair-wide operational board; both office users have the same fair-wide audience. Both superintendents need fair-wide entry access to exercise the specified disqualification and disputed-reweigh functions. No per-superintendent assignment is specified.

The specification does not prescribe a separate public board, hide particular entry columns from staff, require consent, or restrict reads to particular statuses. I interpret the office board as the operational entry record, including identifying evidence, eligibility dates, arrival/weighing information, results, and dispute/disqualification information. Entered animals form its arrival queue; weighed and disqualified animals remain operational records. This is a scope interpretation of the brief, not a claim that it explicitly enumerates every office field. No invariant invents a ban on office photographs, weight cards, reasons, placings, or pre-arrival/post-weighing rows. If the intended board is a limited projection, define its field list and lifecycle explicitly and enforce it in the backend; this review does not silently invent that policy.

The same applies to entry details for the owner and the relevant club leaders: the brief grants animals/entries, not just an ear-tag projection. The specification provides no separate confidentiality rule for a disqualification reason or an original weight. Those values still cannot escape the entry's audience, including via image downloads and derived observations. Placings are not public merely because they are results.

Ownership is an enduring resource relationship: removing an exhibitor's role is not specified to revoke access to their existing animals. A signed-in owner can therefore continue to read those entries. Current leader/club, office, and superintendent assignments must be checked on every server read; a former staff role cannot retain staff authority through an old grant. There is no offline sync in this schema. No age, consent, release, or expiry policy is invented from the youth-show setting.

The auxiliary roles table is not a product roster. Keeping each user's own role/club visible to them, with administrative visibility and writes reserved for the credentialed service:operator seat, is a supporting implementation policy consistent with real authentication and protected authority. SPEC.md does not explicitly demand role-record confidentiality or name an operator role. These assertions preserve a reasonable existing provisioning boundary rather than presenting it as an extra product requirement. The service seat is included explicitly in intent and is not assumed exempt. It receives no animal read or write privilege merely from being the operator.

## Questionnaire answers: rows, each column, and lifecycle

This matrix answers every row and column question generated in snapback/generated/security-invariants.q.draft. Each row below applies independently to all five generated audiences; the operator column additionally covers the implemented service seat. “Own” means owner = viewer; “club” means a current leader with roles.club = animals.club; “all” means fair-wide records. A caller with neither a role nor a resource relationship has no animal access. If that caller owns an existing animal, the ownership relationship still applies. Role holders with an additional ownership relationship retain their owner access. An ordinary signed-in caller never inherits the operator seat.

Every admitted read below is permitted in entered, arrived, weighed, and disqualified states. An optional value may be absent before its relevant event; absence is not permission for a wider audience to learn whether that event occurred. There is no consent condition in SPEC.md.

| Animal target | No role or relationship | Exhibitor | Leader | Office | Superintendent | Operator without another grant |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
''')

## Questionnaire answers: authority and integrity

| Effect question | Answer and independent intent |
|---|---|
| animals.insert | A currently provisioned exhibitor registers their own animal. No leader, office user, superintendent, or operator registers on another user's behalf. animals.insert constrains both caller role and owner relationship. Registration copies the caller's provisioned club. The caller cannot appoint themselves exhibitor or choose another owner/club through the authored operation. |
| animals.update | The operational writers are the barn office for arrival/initial weighing and the superintendent for disqualification/disputed reweigh. No exhibitor/leader edits exist in the described workflow. animals.update declares the broad writer set; the operation/column assertions below constrain exclusive powers. The spec does not expressly assign placing authorship; the existing superintendent-only assignPlacing behavior is an implementation choice, not independently promoted to a new exclusive spec requirement. |
| animals.delete | No delete workflow is specified; deleting evidence would conflict with keeping the original weight and reason. Preserve denial with animals.delete only deny. A future retention/deletion feature needs an explicit policy. |
| roles.insert | Only credentialed service:operator provisions a role/club for a chosen principal. Ordinary account signup does not confer authority. |
| roles.update | Only that operator can change role/club assignments. No role can promote itself, appoint a peer, or self-claim another club. The service's recipient choice is trusted administration, not an invitation flow specified by this app. |
| roles.delete | Only that operator may revoke role records. Revocation must stop staff access on subsequent server reads. Existing owner access remains as explained above. |

The existing operation assertions for disqualify and reweigh express the explicit “only the livestock superintendent” requirement and are retained. The existing registerAnimal, recordArrival, and weighIn assertions express the chosen operational division and are retained. Added originalWeight, reweighReason, and dqReason update assertions protect the evidence fields across operations. They deliberately use update rather than write: exhibitors create entries with those optional fields absent, which must not require superintendent authority. The status update assertion permits only the superintendent to move into or edit a disqualified record; office arrival/weigh-in transitions remain permitted. The old-and-next-image meaning is intentional: no office operation is specified on an already disqualified animal.

The required photo and weight card get non-null integrity assertions. A disqualified record must retain a non-null reason. A stored original weight and a reweigh reason must occur together. Text minimums in the schema make a present reason nonblank. These implications capture stored-state obligations, not the full history requirement.

The 90-day tagging boundary is measured at entry, not at read time. The health certificate's 30-day boundary is measured at arrival, not at registration or a later read. Do not hide old records when these intervals elapse. The authored mutations compare server now and use inclusive boundaries, so exactly 90 days and exactly 30 days are admitted. taggedAt and healthCertAt are caller-supplied claimed evidence dates; the backend cannot establish real-world document authenticity just from timestamps. The schema makes those dates and images immutable after entry. This review does not invent a historical-date prohibition beyond the stated eligibility rules.

Exact date arithmetic and cross-operation preservation of the first pre-dispute weight are not expressible with the documented simple invariant predicate vocabulary. They remain explicit review obligations rather than tautological declarations. The authored reweigh operation saves a.originalWeight ?? a.weight, retaining the first original weight through repeated reweighs, and requires a nonblank reason. It stores only the latest reason: if “the reason kept” is intended to require a history of every dispute, an append-only dispute record is needed. The brief does not explicitly specify multiple-dispute history, so this review flags that limitation without claiming such a history exists or weakening the first-original-weight requirement.

A blanket weight-update-only-superintendent assertion would incorrectly forbid the barn office's initial weigh-in. Likewise, setting status "'!= disqualified on every animal update would incorrectly forbid the superintendent'"'s disqualification. The declarations avoid those mistakes. The exclusive named-operation declarations remain necessary; broad table update authority alone does not prove those exclusive operations.

## Verification results and recommendations

Results will be recorded here after the requested command loop completes. Commands are bounded with timeout, run from this directory, and full stdout/stderr is preserved without truncation in the requested files.
''')

This review uses SPEC.md, the authored snapback/schema.q, the installed package README, and installed CLI guides start, security --full, testing --full, rules --full and language --full. No other application or package implementation was consulted. Only single-line invariant declarations in the authored schema were replaced or added. Rules, operations, schedules, authentication, comments and other existing bytes are unchanged. Existing comments are preserved as required; their policy claims are not independent specification evidence.

## Independent interpretation

The explicit privacy boundaries are the homeowner's own address/results/photos, the contractor's assigned addresses, and the crew's scheduled/finished job map. Crew membership alone does not authorize noticed, refused or rescheduled homes. In the existing vocabulary, scheduled is scheduled; replaced, sampled and sampleSkipped are finished replacement jobs. A sampling skip is not itself proof of sampling. No per-crew assignment is specified, so two different crew users may see the same eligible map jobs. Contractors must not see another contractor's assignments and homeowners must not see another homeowner's homes. Relationships are checked against the current resource, with current role checks: a stored assignment alone must not retain a former contractor's access. A roleless user receives no business data, even if an obsolete relationship remains.

The specification does not separately spell out readership of agreement metadata, staff identifiers, refusal reasons or contractor/crew access to child records. For these underspecified details I use one bounded operational interpretation: child records and associated metadata follow the same address audience, crews remain limited to eligible jobs, and the program manager may oversee all program records. “Only the addresses assigned” is interpreted as a row boundary, not permission to read just the address text and nothing else. This is an explicit interpretation, not a claim that the specification expressly grants interior-photo or sample-result access to contractors. A narrower column policy would need product clarification; the confirmed row and lifecycle limits remain independently asserted regardless. There is no stated separate curb/interior read audience, consent-based expiry of existing photos, or post-completion expiry for owners/assigned contractors, so none is invented.

Role administration is implementation support for real authenticated users, not a newly inferred manager power: the dedicated trusted operator may provision roles; ordinary accounts, including managers, may not appoint themselves or others. Users may inspect their own role; managers may inspect the roster as oversight. The operator service seat has no implicit business-data readership and is included explicitly in grant-write intent. The privileged system/job boundary remains a separate proof limitation. Current-role checks are chosen to prevent the stale-assignment pattern discussed in the installed security guide.

## Questionnaire answers: every role and column

The following matrix answers every read question in generated/security-invariants.q.draft. Each listed column has its own column-read invariant as well as a whole-row invariant; the latter also protects logical existence. The same audience applies to value-dependent counts, existence, ordering, filters, copied/derived values and downloads. No authored aggregate/view is present. IDs and foreign references are assessed even where the questionnaire omits synthetic IDs.

H = current homeowner, matching this home's homeowner, in any lifecycle state. T = current contractor, matching this home's contractor, in any lifecycle state. C = current crew, for homes in scheduled/replaced/sampled/sampleSkipped only. M = current manager, all program homes. For child tables H/T/C refer to their current parent home. R = only the caller's own role row; managers may see every role row. None means no row, column, download or derived-value permission. An assignment removal immediately removes T from the permitted server audience; a role change removes role-dependent access. Signing deadlines do not revoke an owner's access to already existing information.

| Table / individually assessed columns | Homeowner | Contractor | Crew | Manager | Signed-in, no role/relationship | Operator seat |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| homes: id, address, homeowner, contractor, status, noticeAt, replacedAt, refuseReason, lat, lng | H | T | C | M | None | None |
| agreements: id, home, signedBy, signedAt | H | T | C | M | None | None |
| photos: id, home, kind, photo, takenBy, takenAt | H | T | C | M | None | None |
| samples: id, home, leadPpb, sampledAt, skipped, skipReason, recordedBy | H | T | C | M | None | None |
| roles: id, principal, role | R | R | R | All role rows | None (no role row exists); an own row is readable if present | Only an own row if present |

The questionnaire also lists photos.kind = curb and photos.kind = interior as audiences. These are photo categories, not authenticated roles: neither grants any authority for any row or column. For both kinds evaluate the actual caller using the matrix. In particular, taking a photo does not confer access to other homeowners' photos, and the photo uploader is not an alternative homeowner/contractor relationship.

Every homes.status question has an explicit answer: noticed, refused and rescheduled exclude C; scheduled, replaced, sampled and sampleSkipped admit C. H/T/M do not depend on status. Agreements and sample skips do not widen audiences. No universal public audience exists.

| Table | Insert authority | Update authority | Delete authority |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| roles | Operator service seat, never a self-claimed app role | Operator only, including role/principal columns | No described deletion workflow |

| agreements | Home's current homeowner, signing as self, within 30 days of notice | No described amendment workflow | No described deletion workflow |
| photos | Current crew, recorded as that crew user, required verified image | No described replacement/edit workflow | No described deletion workflow |
| samples | Current crew records actual result as self; manager alone creates skip as self with reason | No described amendment workflow | No described deletion workflow |

The deny update/delete declarations preserve the narrow described workflow; they are not a claim of an explicit perpetual-retention requirement. Managers' general access does not authorize them to create signed homeowner agreements or impersonate crews. There is no contractor write workflow in the specification. The manager determines assignments; a recipient cannot nominate themselves. Current role and resource relationship must be validated, including the chosen contractor's role. Homeowner ownership, contractor assignment and refusal reasons are protected by column-write invariants so a broad crew home update rule cannot silently acquire administrative authority. Operation-specific markRefused and skipSampling intent expresses manager authority without incorrectly forbidding every crew edit to a row that was already refused/skipped under both-image update semantics.

Independent event-time declarations require a signature by notice + 30 days and a non-skipped sample between replacement and replacement + 90 days. A skip must have a reason and no pretended sample result/time; an actual sample must have a result and time. A refused home needs a reason; completed replacement states need a replacement timestamp. Completion requires a signed agreement and both curb/interior evidence, because the described work includes photographing both old-pipe locations. These are specification assertions, not claims that the checker supports every expression. The photo-evidence operation invariant currently has an unsupported index/probe reduction and the time expressions have unsupported arithmetic/live-reference reductions; they deliberately remain declared and unproved.

The 90-day requirement is an obligation to obtain a sample, not merely permission to refuse late writes. Likewise eventual overnight rescheduling is not proof of an exact deadline transition. Temporal liveness and complete state-transition correctness need further evidence beyond these single-row/operation assertions.

## Recommended enforcement work (not applied)

1. Narrow crew reads on homes and all associated child tables to the scheduled/finished lifecycle audience. Apply the policy in backend rules, including homeDetail, homePhotos, homeSample, agreementFor and jobBoard paths, not just map display filters. Do not leave broad child rules as an alternate read channel.
2. Bind ownership/assignment access to current roles and current parent relationships. Retain the independently confirmed same-role isolation boundaries when roles or assignments change. The existing child rules allow a stored homeowner/contractor relationship without a current-role requirement.
3. Give crew writes only the administrative fields they actually need. The existing whole-row update rule permits crew updates without column restrictions; homes.homeowner, homes.contractor and homes.refuseReason write intent cannot be established from that rule alone. Existing named operations appear narrower, so a broad rule is not by itself a demonstrated exploit through an exposed mutation.
4. Preserve the leading manager guards on refusal/skip operations and require their reasons. Preserve server now for signature, replacement and sample timestamps. Validate chosen principals' roles when creating homes as well as when assigning contractors; createHome currently accepts an arbitrary homeowner principal.
5. Require both curb and interior photos before accepting replacement completion. recordReplacement currently checks an agreement but not either photo. A required image in an individual photo row proves neither that a photo row exists nor that both locations were documented.
6. Reconcile deadline semantics. signAgreement and recordSample compare server now against the deadline, which is useful. rescheduleOverdue runs daily at 03:00, so an unsigned address can remain noticed/scheduled after the 30-day limit until the sweep. A replaced home can remain unsampled indefinitely, and the current late-sample refusal does not satisfy the affirmative 90-day requirement. Enforce deadline-sensitive actions and report/handle missed obligations without recording a fake sample or silently permitting a non-manager skip.
7. Verify real-password operation and at least two distinct users of every named role. No persona switch was added. Generated in-memory users exercise role/ownership checks, but alone do not establish a deployed application with eight independently authenticated password accounts. No fixture or account files could be added under this measurement's invariant-only restriction.

## Validation

Results and limitations are recorded below after the final check → test --fixture-only → audit loop. Complete output is retained in check.json, test.txt and audit.json. Successful compilation is not a security proof. Unsupported obligations and nonzero commands are retained rather than weakening intent.
'''
Path('REVIEW.md').write_text(review)
print('Wrote REVIEW.md with complete role/column matrix and write/lifecycle answers.')
